feedback: Reject: the table-selection SPARQL is not faithful to tableModel. It assigns B/AH for all 10< thickness <=35 in PC6-7 only, and D/DH for PC1-5, but the 10-15 mm rows require B/AH for material class one in PC1-5; it also assigns FH to material class three PC4-5 for 40< thickness <=45, where the table requires EH, and marks normal-strength material class three PC4-5 as NOT_APPLICABLE above 40 mm although 40-45 mm requires E. Correct every thickness/polar-class/material/strength branch and boundary. Also enforce that actualHullStructuralSteelGrade belongs to the grade family of the selected steelStrengthCategory before comparing ranks; numeric ranks alone allow cross-family grades to pass. Add the requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade constraint with conditional existence and maxCount 1 (or an equivalent explicit cardinality check): the OPTIONAL pattern can accept one correct value among multiple values and does not robustly enforce the applicable result obligation. Remove the unbound ?undefinedExpected fallback and make unsupported selector combinations fail explicitly.

feedback:
Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Unapproved external/generated IRI(s): http://qudt.org/schema/qudtQuantityValue, http://qudt.org/schema/qudtnumericValue, http://qudt.org/schema/qudtunit
Semantic validator feedback: Repair the malformed QUDT IRIs causing deterministicValidation.valid=false: use the evaluator-registered QUDT namespace/terms consistently for QuantityValue, numericValue, and unit, including inside SPARQL, rather than concatenating http://qudt.org/schema/qudt with local names. Add requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade to the case shape with conditional applicability and maxCount 1 (and minCount 1 whenever the selected Table 8 row is applicable). Replace the current selection logic: its valid-selector branch only checks existence of an arbitrary required grade, so an incorrect result can pass, and its invalid-selector fallback does not faithfully implement the table. Encode every tableModel thickness boundary and polar/material/strength branch, explicitly reject unsupported selectors, require exactly the selected required grade for applicable rows, require no grade for NOT_APPLICABLE rows, and enforce that actual and required grades are in the same steelStrengthCategory before comparing ranks. Preserve the prior corrections: fix the 10–15 mm PC1–5 material-class-one B/AH row, the 40–45 mm material-class-three PC4–5 EH/normal-strength row, and all other table branches and boundaries; remove any undefined fallback and ensure duplicate or missing results fail.

Reject: the table-selection constraint remains semantically incorrect. Do not collapse the 10<thickness<=25 range: 10-15 mm uses B/AH for material class one, while 15-25 mm uses D/DH. For 25-35 mm, material class two requires E/EH for PC1-5 and D/DH for PC6-7; the current branch assigns D/DH to both groups. For 40-45 mm, material class three requires E/EH for PC1-5, B/AH for PC6-7, and is applicable for normal strength PC1-3; the current branch incorrectly permits NOT_APPLICABLE there, assigns FH to high-strength PC1-3, and assigns E/EH to PC6-7. Encode every table row and exact exclusive thickness boundary, reject unsupported selector combinations, require exactly one required grade for applicable rows and no result for NOT_APPLICABLE rows. Preserve the existing correct family-scoped actual-versus-required rank comparison and cardinality constraints.
